newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Australian bond yields up modestly, big week ahead.
newsitem.headline: Australian bond yields up modestly, big week ahead.

text.p: *Australian bond yields ended modestly higher after a more subdued session as the market squared up after this week's strong rally in preparation of next week's key events.
*"Living wage" verdict due Tuesday, CPI on Wednesday.
Australian bond yields ended modestly higher after a more subdued session, as the market squared up after this week's strong rally in preparation of next week's key events.

Traders said the market was always going to be prone to profit-taking after this week's strong rally, but this is likely to resume as it gears up for the "living wage" verdict due Tuesday and the March quarter CPI on Wednesday.
"The market is looking a bit tired after this week's rally, but if we get a modest "living wage" claim of A$12 per week or less it's likely to get fired up again," one traders said.

Anticipation of a modest outcome from the Australian Industrial Relations Commission and a benign inflation report saw long-dated bond yields drop around 30 basis points since last Friday, before the market started winding back today.

There is some speculation that if next week's events go to plan and average weekly earnings on May 1 show wage growth remaining contained, the RBA may have room to ease policy if it feels that recovery is not progressing fast enough.
A Reuters poll of economists taken on Friday gave a 25 percent chance of a further cut in official interest rates in this cycle.

The local market finally gave up some ground to U.S. after this week's strong outperformance, although spreads still remain below levels seen a week ago as domestic bonds went some way to decouple from the current woes of the U.S.
